hero.label: For funders, landowners and partners
hero.title: Land based learning campuses where kids, makers and artists build regenerative communities
hero.subtitle: Greenfire is built to turn a piece of land and a community's real needs into a working campus: a youth academy and maker space, a media and music studio, regenerative land systems and a council that decides together. We will build wherever the land is best and the chance to work with kids, education and regenerative practice lines up. Central Texas is one candidate location among several.

status.title: Where we are, honestly
have: Early revenue from AI services run through Greenfire: workshops, one to one onboarding and AI dashboard builds for artists and small businesses

Working software we built ourselves and can demonstrate: BioRegional OS, an open source platform for a bioregional commons, plus Civil X for tasks and proof of work, Festival OS and our own operator dashboards
A complete plan set: academy and maker space, campus and site selection, financial model, governance, impact framework, market and funding research
Jordan Larsen tours as a musician and runs events, which is how Greenfire plans to gather people
not_yet: No land, lease or site is signed yet. We are choosing the first site
No investors, grants, partners or fiscal sponsor are committed yet
Greenfire's entities are still to be formed. The nonprofit arm will start under a fiscal sponsor
The academy has early interest from a first survey of 4 families. The next step is a paid pre sale

loop.title: How a Greenfire campus works
loop.intro: Every campus will run the same loop. A real local need goes in. A built solution, a story and a funded next project come out.
steps: Community intake and council name the real needs
Water, soil, heat, food and energy data set the priorities
Youth, makers, artists and elders design the response together
The maker space and land team build the smallest useful version
The media studio documents it as film, music and lessons
Events and shows bring people in and raise funds
20% of event net revenue goes to a community project fund the members vote on
Impact is tracked openly, and what works becomes a toolkit for the next site

campus.title: What we build on each site
campus.intro: A wheel around a Council Fire. We build the weekly rhythm first and the buildings second.
zones: The decision room: weekly council, project proposals, participatory budgeting, conflict repair.
Week long camps and year round programs where kids learn by building real things on real land, plus maker memberships for adults outside camp hours.
Podcast, film, recording and livestream. It documents every project and earns from studio and production services.
Food forest, gardens, rain catchment, compost, shade and outdoor classrooms. The land is the classroom and the research lab.
Movement, breath and community care, so the people doing the work stay well.
Stage, fire circle and market space. Events are the cash flow engine and the front door.

location.title: Where we build
location.intro: Greenfire is not tied to one city. We score candidate sites and build where the land and the opportunities are strongest. More than one site over time is the plan: each one is a chapter.
criteria: Land, water and soil quality, and the site's climate risks (heat, flood, fire, drought)
Price or partner terms, so the land does not eat the program budget
Kids nearby: schools, homeschool groups and families looking for programs
A regenerative ecosystem to work with: farms, land projects, eco villages, educators
Rules that allow youth camps, events and lodging without years of permits
Access, and a funder and community ecosystem that wants this to exist
location.candidates: Central Texas is our most fully worked example, and it is one candidate on equal footing with others: the Southwest and Mountain West (California, Arizona, Utah, Colorado) and existing eco village and land project sites where a landowner partner wants a campus. The site that scores best wins.

academy.title: Greenfire Academy
academy.intro: In our first small survey of 4 families, kids wanted to make games, music and videos, and parents wanted confidence, real world skills and time in nature. The academy is designed to give both: real life is the game engine.
points: Every module runs Experience, Translate, Create, Share, and is designed to end with something the child made: a game, a track, a film, a garden system
Flagship programs: Game Creator Lab, Beat Lab, Creator Studio, Survival Builder Lab, Fire Kitchen Lab, and hybrids like Build Your World, where kids map the land and turn it into a playable game

Week long summer camps come first. In our first parent survey, every family that answered picked week long summer camps, and none picked weekend workshops. The sample was small, so the next step is a paid pre sale
Safety and licensing are designed in from day one: background checks, trained staff, guardian consent for any photo or video, and state youth camp licensing where it applies
Teens 14 to 18 can grow into a paid apprentice crew for Greenfire media and builds

phases.title: The phased plan
phases.intro: Each phase has to prove itself before the next is funded. We do not buy the dream before the engine runs.
rows: Entities and fiscal sponsor, the first site shortlist, intake, first council and first event plan
First camps and events on a partner site, first community project, first impact report
Media and maker labs running, monthly councils and events, year round youth programs
Land based campus with gardens, water systems, outdoor classrooms and event capacity
Permanent flagship held in a land trust, the model ready to copy to the next site

model.title: The three year model
model.note: This is a planning model built on Central Texas example costs, not a forecast. It assumes a leased or partner hub and diversified revenue. Year one is the cost of proving the engine.
model.streams: Revenue comes from many streams so no single one carries the hub: memberships, events and shows, media services, studio and maker rentals, camps and workshops, grants and sponsors, products and consulting.

money.title: How the money moves
money.split_title: Every event's net revenue is split the same way
structure: Earned revenue: media, events, studio services, AI services, products
Youth programs, community projects and grants. Starts under a fiscal sponsor
Land trust (a later layer, formed only when land is in play)
Would hold land long term so the community is not priced out of the value it creates
money.credits: Members earn Greenfire credits for verified work. Credits unlock studio time, tools and workshops. They are not money, not tradable and never a vote. Governance is one member, one voice.

impact.title: What we will measure
impact.intro: Targets, not results. Greenfire has not yet run a hub. Each site measures its own baseline in its first 90 days, ecological targets scale to what that site makes possible, and any percentage on fewer than 10 people is reported as a count.
targets: Youth confidence gain, self rated before and after
Event net paid to artists, creators and crew
Community project fund deployed by member vote
Rain captured, as a share of what each site's catchment can harvest
Volunteer hours as a share of project hours, so no one works unpaid by default
New members who reach a first real result within 14 days

ways.title: Ways to take part
items: Fund Phase 0 and the first pilot. Donations will go through a fiscal sponsor once one is signed.
Host an event, a six month pilot hub, or a full chapter. No land transfer is needed to start.
Fund a camp cohort, scholarships, the maker space or the media lab.
Youth education, creative workforce, environmental education and climate resilience programs.
Later phases only: equipment, buildout and land, once the pilot has operating proof.
ways.legal: Greenfire is not offering or accepting investments. Its entities are not yet formed, and donations earn no return. Any future loan or investment would be offered only through separate documents prepared by securities counsel, to eligible persons where the law allows. The figures on this page are a planning model and targets, not a forecast or a promise.

contact.title: Request the full plan set
contact.body: The full plan set includes the academy and maker space plan, campus and site selection plan, financial plan with a working model, governance and risk, impact framework, and market and funding research. Write to Jordan and say a little about you and what interests you. He will send you an access code for the private data room, where every document can be read and downloaded.
